gaps.quote: multiplying by $-\varepsilon_w$ again removes the sign
gaps.note: The forward route multiplies by eps_w, so cancelling it needs a factor eps_w (= 1/eps_w), not -eps_w. Multiplying eps_w by -eps_w gives -1, so the sign is not removed (it is introduced when eps_w=+1).

gaps.term: cited endpoint operator for scratch roles
gaps.quote: Every role keeps the endpoint operator (cited), auxiliary roles included.
gaps.note: The page does not say what 'keeps the endpoint operator' states or why it applies. It also seems to conflict with the claim that every auxiliary value is restored: a scratch route applies D_sink D_source^{-1}, which is the identity only if the source and sink frames agree, and the page never states or justifies that.

gaps.quote: its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through
gaps.note: By the page's own result a route applies eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, so with source frame I the operator is eps_w D_nu. It equals D_nu only when the sign is +1 (as for a scratch role), which the example does not say.
